More details on the nature of fake review transactions are detailed in He et al (2022a). This data can be used to study the characteristics (linguistics or otherwise) of fake vs real reviews and to assess proposed fake review detection methods."

resources.name: Illinois Educator Supply and Demand Data
resources.description: "This page ​contains enhancements for the triennial Educator Supply and Demand Report required per School Code [105 ILCS 5/2-3.11c]. The data here addresses the relative supply and demand for education staff in Illinois public schools. The PDF version of the reports can also be found below.  The data is sourced from ISBE, the Employee Information System (EIS), Educator Licensure Information System (ELIS), and Student Information System (SIS). Those data collections and surveys collect data from school districts throughout the state on at least an annual basis and much more frequently in some cases. Specifically, this data provides information on: the relative supply and demand for teachers, administrators, and other licensed  and non-licensed personnel by field, content area, and levels; state and regional analyses of fields, content areas, and levels with an over/undersupply of educators; and projections of likely high/low demand for educators in a manner sufficient to advise the public, individuals, and institutions regarding career opportunities in education.​​"

resources.name: NCTQ District Policy Pathfinder
resources.description:
"District Policy Pathfinder aims to address these challenges. Pathfinder, formerly the NCTQ Teacher Contract Database, brings together curated, standardized, and verified datasets for 133 large school districts with 112 metrics across seven policy topic areas such as teacher salaries, collective bargaining and contracts, teacher benefits, evaluation, and more. 


The data is structured to support cross-district comparisons and longitudinal analysis going back to 2014-15 on key metrics. The data is transparently coded and documented with a clear, consistent methodology, making it easier to verify. With new data released annually, the sample will continue to grow.


Researchers can download directly from the Explore the Data tool and export to CSV for use in Stata, R, Python, or other analytic tools. A full data dictionary details answer options and definitions for each metric. Datasets are designed to integrate with other sources, and even include NCES IDs, to extend your analysis."

resources.name: The Social Determinants of Health Project
resources.description: "Finding data about the Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) and community context is tough. The data is often scattered, hard to find, and takes time to learn how to use, especially when it involves integrating geospatial data and then transforming for analysis and communications. The SDOH & Place Project was created to make this process easier. A human-centered design approach centers everything we do around the diverse range of people who need access to this critical SDOH data. With a multidisciplinary team, we’ve crafted multiple resources to help researchers and advocates to explore and understand SDOH data and generate high impact research and advocacy centered in health equity. "

resources.description: "Illinois Open Data Portal lets you find data across state, find facts about your state, lets you create maps and graphs, and lets you freely download the data for your own analysis. Many of these datasets are updated daily, and some even more often. On March 10, 2014, the Illinois General Assembly unanimously passed PA 98-0627, a bill introduced by the Governor's Office and intended to increase transparency, accountability and savings in government by establishing a new State Open Operating Standard. On December 10, 2018 HB1168 was enacted extending the repeal date for the Open Operating Standards Act to January 21, 2021. We are excited to provide this service and are working hard to make it more useful. New to the open data portal? Navigate over to the quick start guides. If you have any questions or feedback, email us."

That information and other data is used to create a number of reports that provide information about a variety of topics, such as student performance, spending and implementation of legislation."

start_here.name: Common Core of Data
start_here.useful: Describing and counting public schools and districts: enrollment by grade and student group, staff counts, school type, location, and district finances. Most other K-12 datasets link to it.
start_here.row: A public school, district, or state in a given school year.
start_here.getting_started: Download files by year from NCES, or get cleaned, stacked years from the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal.
start_here.years: Annual, from the mid-1980s to the present.
start_here.structure: Yearly files that link across years by NCES school and district IDs.

start_here.name: Civil Rights Data Collection
start_here.useful: Discipline, course access (e.g., AP and calculus), staffing, chronic absenteeism, restraint and seclusion, and harassment, broken out by race, sex, disability, and English learner status.
start_here.row: A public school (some items are reported by district).
start_here.getting_started: Download the files for a collection year from the CRDC site, then join to CCD by NCES school ID.
start_here.years: Every other school year. All public schools since 2011-12; most recently 2023-24.
start_here.structure: Snapshots every two years. Questions change between collections, so check comparability.

start_here.name: The Educational Opportunity Project at Stanford University
start_here.useful: Comparing average test scores (grades 3-8, math and reading) across districts, counties, and schools, including across states that use different tests.
start_here.row: A district, county, or school; the detailed files have one row per place, year, grade, and subject.
start_here.getting_started: Download from the Educational Opportunity Project's Get the Data page after accepting the data use terms. The pooled files are the easiest place to start.
start_here.years: Main release about 2009 to 2019; later releases compare district scores in 2019, 2022, and 2023.
start_here.structure: A panel of places over years and grades.

start_here.name: National Education Research Database on Schools (NERD$)
start_here.useful: School-by-school per-pupil spending, which states have reported under federal law since 2018-19.
start_here.row: A school in a fiscal year.
start_here.getting_started: Download from Edunomics Lab. States count spending differently, so check comparability before comparing across states.
start_here.years: Cleaned files for fiscal years 2019-2022 for every state, with raw state files for some later years.
start_here.structure: Yearly files, linkable to CCD by NCES school ID.

start_here.name: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS)
start_here.useful: Enrollment, admissions, tuition and aid, graduation rates, degrees by field, staff, and finances for every college that takes federal student aid.
start_here.row: A college (institution) in a given year.
start_here.getting_started: Use the IPEDS Data Center's complete data files or custom data files, or the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal.
start_here.structure: Yearly survey components that link across years by college ID (UNITID).

start_here.name: College Scorecard
start_here.useful: Student debt, loan repayment, and earnings after college, overall and by field of study.
start_here.row: A college in a given year, or (in the field-of-study files) a college, credential level, and field.
start_here.getting_started: Download the "most recent" files for a quick look, or all years. A free API key gives programmatic access.
start_here.years: Institution files from 1996-97 to the present; field-of-study files cover recent pooled cohorts only.
start_here.structure: Yearly institution files; debt and earnings are measured for pooled groups of students, not individuals.

start_here.name: American Community Survey
start_here.useful: Characteristics of people and places: income, poverty, educational attainment, school enrollment, language, and more, down to census tracts.
start_here.row: A geographic area (in published tables), or a person or household (in the public use microdata).
start_here.getting_started: Get tables from data.census.gov or the tidycensus R package. For individual-level data, use IPUMS USA.
start_here.years: Annual since 2005; 5-year estimates for small areas.
start_here.structure: Repeated snapshots; the same people aren't followed over time.

start_here.name: IPUMS
start_here.useful: Individual-level census and survey data made consistent across years and countries, including the ACS, US censuses, and the Current Population Survey.
start_here.getting_started: Create a free account, then build an extract by choosing samples and variables. The ipumsr package reads extracts into R; Stata files are also offered.
start_here.years: Varies by collection; US census samples go back to 1850.
start_here.structure: Mostly repeated snapshots; some Current Population Survey records can be linked across months.

start_here.name: Urban Institute's Education Data Portal/Explorer
start_here.group: One place for several of these
start_here.useful: Getting CCD, CRDC, IPEDS, College Scorecard, and other federal education data already cleaned and stacked across years, with consistent variable names.
start_here.row: A school, district, or college in a given year, depending on the source.
start_here.getting_started: Point and click in the Data Explorer, or use the educationdata packages for R and Stata, or the API.
start_here.years: As far back as each source goes; CCD from the 1980s.
start_here.structure: Panels that link across sources and years by NCES IDs.
